correctness.rationale: The projective stabilizer proof is correct. Degree preservation separates the two conic components from the three lines, and tangency versus secancy intrinsically distinguishes the two conics, so both conics are fixed individually. Restriction to the inner conic embeds the stabilizer into the permutation group of the three line-tangency points; the kernel is trivial because a conic automorphism fixing three points is identity and a plane projectivity fixing a nondegenerate conic pointwise is scalar. The displayed matrices R and S preserve both conics, cyclically permute or reflect the three lines, and satisfy the dihedral relations, so the upper bound S3 is attained. The exact verifier independently checks the matrix relations, conic preservation, line permutation, tangencies, ordinary triple transversality, the two conic intersections at infinity, their orbit behavior, and the complete Bezout count.
